stories.headline: [NPR] Lead negotiator on 2015 Iran nuclear deal weighs in on what's next for Trump's deal NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Wendy Sherman, the lead U.S. negotiator on the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement, about the road ahead for U.S. negotiators aiming to str
stories.summary: Wendy Sherman, the lead US negotiator on the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement, shared her insights on the road ahead for US negotiators aiming to strike a new deal. The 2015 agreement, known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), was finalized under the Obama administration. Sherman and Robert Malley, another key negotiator, have experience with Iran talks. Malley, who also served as special envoy for Iran under Joe Biden, is helping to make sense of the current conflict. The Trump administration's approach to negotiations is being closely watched, following the first round of talks. The goal is to end the Iran war and establish a new agreement, with US negotiators facing challenges in their efforts to reach a deal. Sherman's expertise and Malley's involvement provide valuable context for understanding the complex negotiations.

stories.headline: [Nine.com.au] US politics, Iran war LIVE updates: Trump at G7 meeting in France; Status of the Strait of Hormuz unknown; Deal to be signed on Friday The peace deal is done, Trump says, but few other details remain.
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has announced that a peace deal with Iran is done, with a signing expected on Friday. The agreement aims to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, providing relief to the global economy. Trump made the announcement while attending the G7 summit in France, where he has been discussing the deal. The US and Iran had previously reached a ceasefire agreement, with Trump calling on both Iran and Israel to stand down. The status of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil shipping route, is expected to be resolved with the deal's implementation. Trump has described negotiations with Iran as "constructive," emphasizing the need for both sides to take their time to get the agreement right. The details of the deal remain scarce, but a signing is anticipated on Friday.

stories.headline: [France 24] In US, Trump's Iran deal receives mixed reception Donald Trump can claim a diplomatic victory after reaching an agreement with Iran to end the war in the Middle East, but numerous pitfalls remain and the US pre
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has announced a diplomatic agreement with Iran to end the war in the Middle East. Trump claims the deal is "all signed" ahead of an official signing ceremony in Geneva. The US will be represented by Vice President JD Vance. However, Tehran says no final decision has been made, and the full text of the deal has not been released, leaving lingering questions. The agreement comes after three months of conflict, which began when Trump launched strikes against Iran following the downing of a US army helicopter. The deal's reception in the US is mixed, with many Americans unconvinced, amid mounting pressure on Trump to end the conflict ahead of midterm elections in November. The details of the agreement are expected to be clarified during the official signing ceremony.

stories.headline: [Euronews.com] 21-year-old woman dies after being launched off bridge without safety rope Viral videos of the tragedy shared online show the anguish of onlookers when they realised the lady was launched off the Ponte do Esqueleto bridge in Brazil wit
stories.summary: A 21-year-old woman, Maria Eduarda Rodrigues de Freitas, died after being launched off the Ponte do Esqueleto bridge in Brazil without a safety rope while participating in a guided bungee jumping event. The incident occurred when two instructors pushed her from the bridge, causing her to fall 130 feet into a ravine below. Viral videos show the moment of the tragedy, with onlookers expressing anguish upon realizing the woman was not attached to a rope. The incident happened on Saturday, and the woman was later buried in São Paulo state. An investigation is likely to follow, focusing on the negligence of the bungee jumping event workers who failed to secure the woman to the safety equipment before pushing her off the bridge. The bridge, known as the "Skeleton Bridge," is a popular spot for adventure activities.

stories.headline: Toys for Bob says Spyro: Reignited's 11m sales proved "there's an audience that woke up to show up for that series"
stories.summary: Toys for Bob has highlighted the success of Spyro: Reignited, which sold over 11 million copies. The studio believes this demonstrates a significant audience for the series, with fans "waking up" to show their support. The game's performance indicates a loyal fan base, with the developer noting that every year and at every gaming event, they hear from fans eager for more Spyro content. The sales figures suggest that the series still has a strong following, prompting Toys for Bob to revisit the franchise. The success of Spyro: Reignited has provided clear evidence of the series' enduring popularity, with the developer acknowledging the audience's enthusiasm and dedication to the brand. This has likely influenced the studio's decision to continue working on Spyro projects.

stories.headline: Forza Horizon 6 June 15 Update Released - Full Patch Notes
stories.summary: Forza Horizon 6 has released a June 15 update with various improvements and fixes. The patch notes include changes to Drag Tire gameplay, improvements to Horizon Play XP, particularly a faster curve from levels 26 to 100, and visual fixes. Additionally, the update addresses issues with unlocking Level 12 in Horizon Play and makes adjustments to Drivatar AI difficulty balancing and race-start behavior. Other fixes include resolving problems with some players not unlocking Level 12 until they entered another race event. The update aims to enhance the overall gaming experience, with version number 364.933 for XBOX Series X|S. The Forza Support Team has also provided release notes for previous updates, including May 27th and May 18th, and a Series 1 Hotfix 2 for Steam, XBOX, and Windows PC.

stories.headline: Audio-Technica unveils AT-MCD1 flagship moving coil cartridge
stories.summary: Audio-Technica has launched its new flagship moving coil cartridge, the AT-MCD1, at the High End 2026 show in Vienna. The cartridge is priced at £9999 or €11,000, making it one of the most expensive options available. Designed as the company's highest expression of analogue engineering and craftsmanship, the AT-MCD1 represents the pinnacle of Audio-Technica's moving coil cartridge technology. The cartridge is available now, with inquiries and more information available on the company's website. The AT-MCD1 is an iron-core, moving-coil stereo cartridge, showcasing Audio-Technica's expertise in analogue audio technology. It is now available for purchase, with further details accessible on the Audio-Technica website at www.audio-technica.com.

stories.headline: The Voigtländer Nokton 35mm f/1.4 Arrives on RF and Z Mount Next Month
stories.summary: Cosina Voigtländer's Nokton Classic 35mm f/1.4 lens is set to arrive on Canon RF and Nikon Z mount next month. The lens is already available in M-mount and E-mount, and its release on the new mounts was first unveiled at CP+ in February. The manual-focus prime lens is known for its versatility and will be softer wide open compared to other lenses. The exact release date and pricing have not been announced yet. The Nokton Classic 35mm f/1.4 has been well-received in its existing mounts, with users praising its performance on cameras such as Sony and Leica. Its upcoming release on RF and Z mount will provide users of Canon and Nikon cameras with a new high-quality lens option. The lens is expected to be available for purchase soon, with more details to be announced in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Marner’s old playoff habits resurface to somewhat let the Leafs off the hook A Conn Smythe lock a week ago, Marner’s productivity fell off, allowing Carolina to reverse its fortunes in the Stanley Cup final
stories.summary: Mitch Marner's productivity has declined in the Stanley Cup final, allowing the Carolina team to reverse its fortunes. Previously considered a lock for the Conn Smythe award, Marner's performance has fallen off. Despite leading the playoffs with 28 points, including 10 goals and 18 assists, his recent play has been disappointing. Marner's teammates on the Toronto Maple Leafs have also struggled in the playoffs. His 28 points surpass the previous record set by Jack Eichel in 2023, when the Vegas Golden Knights won the Stanley Cup. Eichel praised Marner, saying "he's on another level right now." However, Marner's recent decline has impacted the team's performance in the Stanley Cup final. The 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs, which began on April 18, are nearing conclusion, with the final series ending no later than June 21.

stories.headline: 'The ball didn't want to go in!' - Spain boss stands by strategy after Cape Verde pull off stunning World Cup draw against European champions
stories.summary: Spain, the 2010 World Cup winners and European champions, were held to a 0-0 draw by debutants Cape Verde in their 2026 World Cup opener. Despite creating several big chances, Spain failed to score, with coach Luis de la Fuente defending his team's tactics. Cape Verde, considered heavy underdogs, pulled off a stunning result, shutting out the favored Spanish team. The match marked Cape Verde's World Cup debut, and their goalkeeper, Vozinha, was emotional after the final whistle, having faced some of the best players in the world. The draw is considered one of the most surprising results of the tournament so far, with Spain missing out on an expected win against the tiny island nation. The result has raised questions about Spain's strategy, but de la Fuente stands by his team's approach.

stories.headline: World Cup 2026: Spain 0-0 Cape Verde Veteran goalkeeper Vozinha stars and Spain reach 2,500 passes since their last World Cup goal - the key stats as debutants Cape Verde secure a memorable point
stories.summary: Spain and Cape Verde played to a 0-0 draw in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Cape Verde's 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha made seven saves, including several at close range, to help his team secure a memorable point in their World Cup debut. Spain had 27 attempts on goal but were unable to score, extending their drought to 2,500 passes since their last World Cup goal. Vozinha's performance was notable, as he became one of the oldest goalkeepers to make multiple saves in a World Cup match. The draw was a significant achievement for Cape Verde, who were making their first appearance in the tournament. The match was played in Atlanta, with Spain dominating possession but unable to break through Cape Verde's defense.

stories.headline: Arne Slot's Liverpool assistants reunite at Feyenoord as Robin van Persie is replaced by ex-Arsenal star Giovanni van Bronckhorst and Sipke Hulshoff leave Arne Slot's Liverpool staff to take over at Feyenoord following Robin van Persie's departure
stories.summary: Giovanni van Bronckhorst is set to return to Feyenoord as the club's new head coach, replacing Robin van Persie. Van Bronckhorst, a former Feyenoord player and manager, will be joined by Sipke Hulshoff, who is also leaving Arne Slot's staff at Liverpool. The duo's departure follows Arne Slot's own exit, with Van Bronckhorst and Hulshoff tasked with maintaining the high standards set by Slot during his time at Feyenoord. Van Bronckhorst came through the Feyenoord ranks as a player before turning professional in 1993 and later took charge of the team 11 years ago. The new appointments mark the beginning of a new era at Feyenoord, with Van Bronckhorst and Hulshoff aiming to build on the success achieved under Slot's management. Ruben Peeters is also leaving Liverpool to join the new setup at Feyenoord.

stories.headline: Export duty on diesel, ATF hiked with petrol unchanged
stories.summary: The government has increased the export duty on diesel to ₹55.5 per litre and on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) to ₹42 per litre, effective from June 16, 2026. The export duty on petrol remains unchanged at ₹1.5 per litre. The hike in export duty is aimed at securing fuel supply amid price volatility. The increase in export duty on diesel is ₹14 per litre and on ATF is ₹12.5 per litre. Excise duty rates on petrol and diesel for domestic consumption will remain unchanged. The move is intended to prevent domestic fuel shortages by discouraging exports of diesel and ATF, and to stabilize the supply of these fuels in the country. The revised export duties will apply from June 16, 2026.

stories.headline: Govt hikes windfall tax on diesel, ATF; petrol duty unchanged
stories.summary: The Indian government has increased the windfall tax on diesel exports to Rs 14 per litre and on Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) exports to Rs 12.5 per litre, effective June 16. The tax on petrol exports remains unchanged at Rs 1.5 per litre. This move aims to secure fuel supply amid price volatility. The hike in export duty on diesel and ATF will result in higher duties on shipments for exporters. The revision comes after the last change on June 1, which had reduced windfall taxes across all three fuel categories. Domestic excise rates on petrol, diesel, and ATF remain unchanged. The new rates are intended to balance fuel supply and prices in the domestic market. The government's decision is expected to impact exporters and the fuel market, with the revised duties applying from June 16 onwards.

stories.headline: PM Modi conferred Slovakia's highest honour, receives 33rd international award
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been conferred with Slovakia's highest honour, marking his 33rd international award. This recognition follows a series of global honours he has received, including Norway's Grand Cross, Sweden's acknowledgement, and Cyprus's Grand Cross of the Order of Makarios III. Previously, he was awarded Namibia's highest civilian award, the Order of the Most Ancient Welwitschia Mirabilis, in July 2025. Since 2014, PM Modi has received a total of 33 international awards, reflecting India's growing global presence and recognition of his contributions. These awards demonstrate the international community's appreciation for his efforts in advancing bilateral relations and global interests. The latest honour from Slovakia adds to the list of countries that have recognized PM Modi's achievements and India's rising global stature.

stories.headline: Bangladesh PM’s adviser returns from Delhi airport; says he was ‘humiliated’ by immigration
stories.summary: Bangladesh Prime Minister's adviser, Zahed Ur Rahman, was detained at Delhi airport for over two hours by immigration authorities on Sunday. Despite having a valid SAARC visa exemption and prior notification to Indian authorities, Rahman was stopped after his name was flagged during a routine security check. He claimed to have been "humiliated" during the detention. After being held for several hours, Rahman decided not to continue with his visit and returned home via Sri Lanka. The incident prompted Bangladesh to summon India's High Commissioner, seeking an explanation for the treatment of the Prime Minister's adviser. Rahman advises the Prime Minister on Policy and Strategy Affairs as well as Information and Broadcasting. The detention has sparked a diplomatic row between the two countries.

stories.headline: Political Tensions, Visa Woes, Travel Chaos: Challenges Facing Iran At FIFA World Cup 2026
stories.summary: Iran's 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign is facing challenges due to visa issues, travel disruptions, and political tensions. The team's participation has been complicated by geopolitical factors, with FIFA being criticized for the travel chaos affecting the tournament. Iran's fans have also been banned from bringing the lion and sun flag to the SoFi Stadium for their World Cup opener against New Zealand, following an emergency hearing in Los Angeles. A judge ruled that free speech arguments were not sufficient to allow the flag, which has been a point of contention. Meanwhile, other teams, such as Uruguay, have experienced trouble arriving at their destinations, with FIFA being blamed for the disruptions. Iran's players have managed to celebrate on the field, scoring against New Zealand in their Group G match on June 15. The tournament is scheduled to run from June 11 to July 19, 2026.

stories.headline: Rupee gains as geopolitical tensions ease
stories.summary: The Indian rupee gained strength against the US dollar for the third consecutive day, rising 40 paise to close at 94.71, a five-week high. This upward momentum is attributed to easing geopolitical tensions in West Asia, which boosted market sentiment. The decline in the dollar's value also contributed to the rupee's gain. Previously, the rupee had weakened due to rising tensions between the US and Iran, but as concerns eased, the currency regained its footing. The rupee had hovered near 93.2 per dollar earlier, before gaining momentum to reach its current level. The easing of geopolitical tensions has provided support to the currency, leading to its current strength against the US dollar. The rupee's gain is a positive development for the Indian economy, reflecting improved market sentiment.

stories.headline: Geopolitics and sport collide as Iran prepare to play in Los Angeles
stories.summary: Iran's national team is set to play its opening 2026 FIFA World Cup group match against New Zealand in Los Angeles, amidst controversy and protests. The team's arrival in the city has been overshadowed by visa issues, travel disruptions, and political tensions. The match has become a focal point for opponents of the Iranian government, with many gathering outside the stadium waving the Lion and Sun flag, a symbol of resistance to the current regime. The event is testing how a major sporting event can navigate geopolitical strain without letting it overtake the match. Protests and drama are expected to accompany the game, highlighting the complex intersection of football and geopolitics in a community with emotional ties to Iran and its ongoing conflicts. The stadium is preparing for a potentially volatile situation.

stories.headline: Fable 5 shutdown exposes geopolitics of AI access, risks of dependence
stories.summary: The shutdown of Fable 5, an AI model, has sparked global concerns about dependence on AI and sovereign capabilities. The incident has forced companies worldwide, including those in India, to reassess their AI reliance and potential risks. Governments are taking notice, with the shutdown serving as a live example of model-level intervention, prompting regulators to reevaluate their approaches. The move has been criticized as government overreach, citing Fable 5's safety features and potential AI advantages. However, the shutdown has also accelerated sovereign AI efforts globally, with Europe and India now considering AI model access an operational risk. Anthropic, the developer, may bring Fable and its companion model, Mythos, back online, but the incident has already highlighted the geopolitics of AI access and the need for diversified AI capabilities. This has significant implications for the future of AI development and regulation.

stories.headline: India’s Opposition: Stranded Between Alliance and Disarray
stories.summary: India's Opposition INDIA bloc has reaffirmed its commitment to fight against the Modi government in its first meeting after the recent state legislative assembly elections. The meeting, held in Delhi, saw the participation of 23 parties, with some notable absentees, including the DMK and CPI(M), conveying their strong opposition to the government's policies. The bloc's unity has been questioned following electoral losses suffered by some of its key constituents, such as the Aam Aadmi Party and DMK. Despite this, the Congress has sought to project unity, with Jairam Ramesh stating that the coalition remains unified in its ideological opposition to the Central government. The meeting, known as the "Janbandhan" meeting, aims to launch a coordinated fight against the Modi government, amidst concerns of disarray and self-preservation among allies. The bloc's future looks uncertain after recent electoral setbacks.

stories.headline: How Kundu couple could turn nondescript NCPI into 5th-biggest party in Lok Sabha
stories.summary: The Nationalist Congress Party of India (NCPI) is set to become the fifth-biggest party in the Lok Sabha. This development comes after rebel TMC MPs joined the party, driven by political and legal calculations. The NCPI, a six-year-old party from Tripura, is now the second-biggest member of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). The party's growth is significant, surpassing other major parties in the Lok Sabha. The current party standings are: BJP with 240 MPs, Congress with 99 MPs, Samajwadi Party with 37 MPs, and DMK with 22 MPs. The NCPI's rise occurs amidst ongoing disruptions in Parliament due to protests over the SIR issue, which has been ongoing for 13 days, with a brief pause following Shibu Soren's death.

stories.headline: No other headlines are provided to choose from, so I will repeat the given headlines to fill the request
stories.summary: Recent discussions have focused on the importance of accurate and attributed news headlines. Experts recommend that all headlines, both print and online, related to significant topics such as the Trump Administration, must have proper attribution to ensure credibility. The issue of false or misleading headlines has also been highlighted, as they can lead to the spread of incorrect information in comments sections and beyond. Meanwhile, news outlets such as APNews.com continue to provide independent journalism from around the globe, covering a range of topics including current events, Landsat missions, and data product updates. Accurate and concise headlines are crucial in conveying factual information and preventing the dissemination of misinformation. Proper attribution and fact-consistent titles are essential in maintaining the integrity of news reporting.

stories.headline: India’s Opposition: Stranded Between Alliance and Disarray
stories.summary: India's opposition alliance, INDIA, appears to have lost momentum after initially making a strong statement. Despite a heartening performance in the 2024 election, where the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance were challenged on issues like unemployment and economic distress, the opposition alliance has slipped into inactivity. Mayawati's BSP is keeping a distance from the opposition, although there is a push from within the party to join the INDIA alliance. Meanwhile, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has been engaging with youngsters affected by examination paper leaks. Prime Minister Modi has criticized the Congress, stating that it pushed the country into disarray. The opposition's disarray has raised questions about its ability to challenge the ruling BJP effectively. The INDIA alliance's inactivity has sparked concerns about its future and impact on Indian politics.

stories.headline: How Kundu couple could turn nondescript NCPI into 5th-biggest party in Lok Sabha
stories.summary: A husband-and-wife duo, the Kundu couple, is set to transform the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) into the fifth-largest party in the Lok Sabha. The party, currently unrecognised and without any MPs, MLAs, or local body representatives, is expected to merge with nearly 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs. If approved by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the merger would catapult NCPI to the second-largest party in the ruling NDA government. The dramatic turn of events has the potential to significantly boost the party's presence in the Lok Sabha, making it a major player in Indian politics. The NCPI, founded by the Kundu couple from West Bengal, would undergo a significant transformation, gaining substantial representation in the Lok Sabha. The merger's approval is pending, and the Speaker's decision will determine the party's future.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty climb as global markets rally, crude oil prices cool Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rallied in early trade, driven by a positive trend in global markets, cooling crude oil prices following a US-Iran pea
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rallied in early trade, driven by a positive trend in global markets and cooling crude oil prices. The rally follows a peace deal between the US and Iran, which has led to a decline in crude oil prices. Fresh foreign fund inflows have also contributed to the uptrend. The Sensex and Nifty rose in trade, with investor sentiment improving sharply after the announcement of the US-Iran peace framework. The decline in crude oil prices has also boosted market sentiment, as it is expected to have a positive impact on the Indian economy. The peace deal is expected to resume traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, further easing oil prices. The rally in Indian markets is in line with the positive trend in global markets.

stories.headline: Stock markets surge on US-Iran peace deal, oil price drop Indian stock markets extended their gains for a second consecutive session, with the Sensex closing 736 points higher, driven by a global equity rally and a sig
stories.summary: Indian stock markets rose for the second consecutive session, with the Sensex closing 736 points higher at 76,264.33. The surge was driven by a global equity rally and a sharp decline in crude oil prices after the US and Iran finalized a deal to end their 107-day war. The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 736.38 points, or 0.97 per cent, while the 50-share NSE Nifty also saw significant gains. The deal between the US and Iran is expected to open the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway, and has led to a notable decline in crude oil prices. The positive global market trend and renewed foreign fund inflows also contributed to the rally in Indian stock markets, including the Sensex and Nifty. The markets experienced a significant rally in early trade, with the Sensex jumping 1,112.70 points to 76,648.74 in early deals.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty close sharply higher: 5 reasons behind today's stock market surge Indian markets rallied for a second straight session on June 15 after the US and Iran confirmed a deal to end the war, easing geopolitical concerns and triggeri
stories.summary: Indian markets surged for a second consecutive session on June 15, with the Sensex and Nifty closing sharply higher. The rally was driven by easing geopolitical concerns after the US and Iran confirmed a deal to end the war. A ceasefire between Israel and Iran, announced by US President Donald Trump, also contributed to the market surge. Additionally, a sharp decline in global crude oil prices to the $80-$84 range fueled the rally, easing concerns over oil supply disruptions. The strong rally across global markets and rising optimism surrounding the proposed US-Iran peace deal also supported the Indian market's upward trend. The Sensex and Nifty gained ground, reversing earlier losses amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. The ceasefire and deal have boosted investor sentiment, leading to a significant increase in the Indian stock markets.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today | Closing Bell: Sensex, Nifty Surge Over 1%; Investors Gain Rs 9 Lakh Crore Amid US-Iran Peace Optimism Indian markets ended nearly 1 per cent higher as easing US-Iran tensions boosted global sentiment and lowered oil prices. Sensex gained 736 points while Nifty r
stories.summary: Indian stock markets surged over 1% with the Sensex gaining 736 points and the Nifty also rising significantly. The rally was driven by easing US-Iran tensions, which boosted global sentiment and lowered oil prices. This decline in crude prices eased concerns over global inflation, supporting risk assets worldwide. Asian markets, including South Korea's Kospi, Japan's Nikkei 225, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng, posted sharp gains, ranging from 1.7% to 4.6%. European markets and Wall Street also traded higher, with technology stocks leading the rally. The positive movement across global equities contributed to the bullish mood in Indian markets, resulting in investors gaining Rs 9 lakh crore. The rally was further supported by US President Trump's decision to pause some tariffs, leading to a significant increase in high beta stocks.

stories.headline: ASX set to fall, global stocks jump on peace deal; SpaceX rises again
stories.summary: The ASX is expected to fall despite global stocks rising after a US-Iran peace deal was announced. The Australian dollar is trading at US70.68¢. Previously, the ASX jumped 1.3% after the agreement was confirmed, with the S&P/ASX 200 finishing up 110 points, or 1.25%, at 8914. Oil prices declined following the ceasefire announcement. Meanwhile, SpaceX's record IPO closed up 19% on debut, with the stock rising to US$84. The S&P 500 also rose as investors awaited the potential peace deal and the SpaceX IPO. The RBA rates decision is scheduled for tomorrow, which may impact the ASX. Global markets are reacting positively to the peace deal, with Wall Street closing higher, but the ASX is set to fall, contrary to its initial reaction to the agreement.

stories.headline: In High-Risk B-Cell ALL, Swapping Out Chemo for Blinatumomab Improves Outcomes
stories.summary: A phase 3 trial found that adding blinatumomab to chemotherapy improved disease-free survival in children with newly diagnosed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The study, presented at the ASH Annual Meeting, showed that blinatumomab substantially improved outcomes in children with standard-risk B-cell ALL. An interim analysis revealed significant efficacy, leading to early termination of randomization. The trial compared blinatumomab with intensive multidrug consolidation chemotherapy in children with high-risk, first-relapse B-cell ALL. Results showed that blinatumomab reduced toxicity and improved disease-free survival across all subgroups. The study suggests that blinatumomab can be an effective alternative to chemotherapy in some cases, improving outcomes for children with high-risk B-cell ALL. The findings indicate a potential new treatment approach for this patient population.

stories.headline: Jacobs appointed to deliver feasibility study for potential desalination plant in Singapore
stories.summary: Jacobs has been appointed by Singapore's national water agency PUB to deliver a feasibility study for a potential new desalination plant. The study will assess land-optimized and dual-mode desalination designs to support Singapore's long-term water security. Singapore currently has five operational desalination plants, and PUB is exploring the viability of a sixth plant. The feasibility study will determine the capital and operating costs, which will be announced after the study's completion. The project aims to enhance Singapore's climate resilience and ensure a stable water supply. Jacobs will utilize its data science and technology-enabled expertise to deliver the study's outcomes. The appointment is part of PUB's efforts to strengthen Singapore's water security and meet its long-term water needs. The study's findings will inform the development of the potential new desalination plant.

stories.headline: WD-40 Company Declares Regular Quarterly Dividend and Schedules Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call
stories.summary: WD-40 Company has declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.88 per share, payable on July 31, 2026. The company has also scheduled its third quarter 2026 earnings conference call for Thursday, July 9, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. PDT. During the call, management will discuss the company's financial results, business developments, and other matters. This announcement follows the company's standard practice of paying quarterly dividends and hosting earnings conference calls to update investors on its performance. The dividend payment and earnings call are part of the company's regular schedule, with the call providing an opportunity for management to share insights into the company's operations and outlook. The earnings call will be held on July 9, 2026, and the dividend will be paid to shareholders on July 31, 2026.

stories.headline: OpenAI wins dismissal of trade secret lawsuit by Musk's xAI
stories.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit by Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company xAI against rival OpenAI, founded by Sam Altman. The lawsuit accused OpenAI of poaching staff to steal trade secrets. The judge's decision removes a potential obstacle to OpenAI's initial public offering (IPO). The verdict was reached after a jury found that Musk's company waited too long to sue, leading to the dismissal. This ruling marks a victory for OpenAI in one of its legal battles with xAI, which had alleged poaching and theft of trade secrets. The case was decided in a California federal court, with the judge citing the timing of the lawsuit as a key factor in the decision.

stories.headline: OpenAI Urges Treasury to Modernize Computer-Use Tax Credit Rules
stories.summary: OpenAI is urging the US Treasury to modernize computer-use tax credit rules, seeking to expand the eligibility of CHIPS-style tax credits to include AI data centers and server manufacturing. The company also wants to include heavy electrical infrastructure, such as transformers and related steel, in credit eligibility. OpenAI is not asking for direct subsidies or a government "backstop" for its operations, but rather broader tax incentives to support AI infrastructure growth. The company's proposals aim to address the potential economic and societal impacts of artificial intelligence. By expanding tax credits, OpenAI hopes to support comprehensive industrial and tech growth initiatives, echoing the tech industry's widespread calls for government support. The requested changes could have significant implications for the development of AI infrastructure in the US.

stories.headline: Can and should Indian investors get a piece of the biggest artificial intelligence IPOs?
stories.summary: Indian investors are seeking exposure to artificial intelligence (AI) initial public offerings (IPOs), which are expected to be a significant part of the upcoming stock market listing wave in the United States. The US is gearing up for one of the biggest IPO waves in history, led by AI companies. However, for investors in India, getting AI exposure is not easy, but it may be necessary for a well-diversified portfolio. The AI industry is expected to be driven by government funding for its most advanced products. Investors are watching whether Wall Street will embrace the high valuations of AI companies, with some being listed on the Forbes 2026 AI 50 List as the most promising AI businesses. This listing wave presents an opportunity for Indian investors to get a piece of the AI market.

stories.headline: Artificial intelligence (AI) firms have been listing their shares on public bourses left and right this year, from China's Zhipu.ai and Minimax to America's Spa
stories.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence firms Zhipu.ai and MiniMax have listed their shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Zhipu.ai's initial public offering raised HK$4.35 billion, with shares rallying 11.8% in early trade. MiniMax's shares soared 109.1% on their debut, pushing the company's valuation to over HK$103 billion. The listings come amid surging AI listings and regulatory scrutiny on Variable Interest Entities (VIEs). MiniMax used a Cayman-incorporated red-chip VIE structure for its listing. The company's consumer AI applications, including Hailuo AI and Talkie, have gained significant traction in the market. The strong debuts of Zhipu.ai and MiniMax follow a trend of AI firms listing on public bourses, with other companies like SpaceX and OpenAI potentially following suit. The listings highlight the growing interest in AI technology and its potential for growth.
